data.title: Singapore Raises 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to Around 6%
data.description:
(00:00 GMT) *Singapore Revised 3Q GDP +1.5% Adj Q/Q vs +1.1% Earlier Estimate
(00:00 GMT) *Singapore Revised 3Q GDP +6.1% on Year vs +5.4% Earlier Estimate
(00:00 GMT) *Singapore Raises 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to Around 6.0% From 4.5%-5.5% Previously
(00:00 GMT) *Singapore Expects 2027 GDP Growth Forecast of 2.5%-4.5%
(00:15 GMT) Singapore Raises 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to Around 6%

By Amanda Lee

SINGAPORE--Singapore raised its economic growth forecast for the year following stronger-than-estimated third-quarter growth, though it cautioned that global headwinds persist.

Gross domestic product expanded 6.1% in the July-September period from a year earlier, according to revised data released Tuesday. The figure was above the 5.4% advance estimate released in October.

Third-quarter GDP growth was driven by wholesale trade, manufacturing, and finance and insurance sectors, the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry said.

"Growth in the machinery, equipment & supplies segment of the wholesale trade sector, as well as the electronics and precision engineering clusters of the manufacturing sector, was boosted by strong AI-related demand," the ministry said.

For the first three quarters of the year, GDP growth was 6.2%.

The ministry now expects growth of around 6% this year, compared with its previous forecast range of 4.5% to 5.5%. For 2027, the economy is expected to grow between 2.5% and 4.5%.

However, the ministry warned of lingering downside risks to the global economy next year, citing concerns over the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence cycle. Such risks could trigger sharper corrections in global financial markets and potentially spill over into broader economic activity.

On a seasonally adjusted, quarter-over-quarter basis, GDP rose 1.5%, beating the advance estimate of 1.1% but cooling from the revised 1.8% expansion recorded in the second quarter.

Write to Amanda Lee at amanda.lee@wsj.com

data.title: Singapore raises 2026 growth forecast after 6.1% Q3 expansion
data.description:
Singapore upgraded its 2026 economic growth forecast to around 6.0% on Tuesday after posting third-quarter expansion of 6.1% from a year earlier, government data showed.

The July to September growth was higher than an official advance estimate of 5.4% and above the 5.6% expected in a Reuters poll of economists​.

On a quarter-on-quarter, seasonally adjusted basis, gross domestic product expanded by 1.5% in the July-September period, compared with an advance estimate of 1.1% growth.

The Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry now expects 2027 GDP growth to come in at a range of 2.5% to 4.5%.

"Although elevated energy prices have contributed to global inflationary pressures and tighter monetary policy in several economies, on balance, METI’s assessment is that Singapore’s external demand outlook for the year has improved compared to the assessment in August," the ministry said.

In a separate statement, Enterprise Singapore upgraded its non-oil domestic exports forecast to a growth of 30% to 32% in 2026, from 14% to 16% previously.

That was driven primarily by AI-related growth in electronics and specialised machinery as well as support from lumpy exports of the structures of ships and boats.

Singapore had in August upgraded its growth forecast for this year to 4.5% to 5.5%, from a previous range of 2.0% to 4.0%, saying the impact of the Middle East war had been less severe than initially feared while the global AI investment boom had been stronger than expected.

Singapore's key consumer price gauge rose 1.5% in October from a year earlier.

Last month, the central bank kept its monetary settings unchanged in a move that surprised analysts, with inflation risks expected to ease slightly as the AI boom and supply constraints moderate.

data.title: Waratah Minerals Delivers High-Grade Gold Assays from Drilling at Goldenclad Prospect
data.description:
Waratah Minerals has intersected broad zones of shallow high-grade gold mineralisation across multiple lodes in diamond drilling at the Goldenclad prospect within its Spur project in New South Wales.

Drilling tested beneath numerous historic gold workings to investigate the continuity of mineralisation across a high-priority six-kilometre target zone at the margin of the Cargo Intrusive Complex (CIC).

Partial results from hole GCD002 along a previously undrilled zone of outcropping mineralisation known as the Wollard’s Line returned best assays of 10 metres at 12.18 grams per tonne gold from 49m within 17m at 7.35g/t and 20.7m at 0.55g/t gold from 11.3m including 2m at 1.76g/t from 30 m.

Hole GCD003 at the Goldenclad Line delivered 7m at 2.58g/t gold from 51m within 13m at 1.51g/t from 48m, 7m at 5.66g/t gold from 85m within 28m at 1.57g/t from 84m, and 7m at 2.68g/t gold from 137m within 32.3m at 1g/t from 123m.

The district appears to contain multiple mineralised structures associated with the margins of the CIC, with recent exploration supporting the concept of a wider corridor linking Ironclad, Goldenclad, Spur, and Consols.

Scale and Potential

Executive chair Andrew Stewart said the latest results delivered high-grade gold close to surface while providing further evidence of the scale and potential of the broader Goldenclad system.

“While drilling at Goldenclad remains at an early stage, our geological team is systematically defining the controls, continuity and architecture of the mineralised system,” he said.

“GCD002 is particularly significant as the first drill test of the Wollard’s Line and has given us an exciting new high-grade result from a separate mineralised trend that remains open for further testing.”

“GCD003 was designed to test for multiple lodes within the Goldenclad Line and has intersected three significant gold zones within the top 155m.”

“These early results indicate a similar emerging theme to that observed at the Consols and Spur gold zones, being multiple gold-bearing lodes within a broader mineralised system, and provide significant scope to expand the mineralised footprint beyond the current mineral resource estimate.”

$50m Capital Raising

Waratah has received firm commitments to raise $50 million to support an ongoing exploration program aimed at growing the Spur project’s 3.1-million-ounce gold resource.

Strong demand from new and existing institutional, sophisticated, and professional investors will see the company issue 76.9 million new and fully paid ordinary shares priced at $0.65 each.

The funds will underpin more than 100,000m of drilling over the next 12 months using 12 diamond rigs to aggressively pursue resource growth.

“Our immediate focus is to convert this funding into metres drilled and then into additional ounces and ultimately build a substantially larger resource at Spur,” Mr Stewart said.

“At the same time, we will continue metallurgical and geotechnical work and broader exploration across at Ironclad, Goldenclad, Alpine, and Gazzards.”

“The strong support from existing shareholders and a select group of new and long-only global specialist resources investors is a significant endorsement of our strategy and the scale of the opportunity at Spur.”

data.title: CFTC staff advisory says crypto can count toward reserves, not liquidity rule
data.description:
Some cryptocurrency assets can count toward the reserves that trading platforms and clearinghouses must keep on hand, but not toward a separate liquidity requirement, staff at the US commodities regulator said in an advisory on Monday.

Here are the details:

  • Staff in the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk issued the advisory.

  • It applies to swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations.

  • The advisory addresses three CFTC regulations that require these entities to hold enough financial resources to cover at least 12 months of operating costs.

  • The staff said bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins may count toward that requirement "subject to appropriate haircuts."

  • Crypto assets cannot satisfy the separate liquidity requirement because they don't qualify as cash or highly liquid securities under accounting rules, according to the advisory.

  • CFTC said the advisory only reflects the views of staff and does not create new rules or enforceable rights, is not a no-action position, and does not necessarily represent the views of the commission.

data.title: HPE Stock Drops 8% After-Hours As Q1 Outlook Marginally Falls Short Of Expectations
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue climbed 50% year-over-year to $14.5 billion, topping Wall Street estimates of $14.3 billion.
  • HPE projected Q1 revenue outlook between $14 billion to $14.6 billion, marginally lower than the highest Wall Street estimates of $14.7 billion.
  • The cloud infrastructure firm lifted its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to as high as $63.1 billion.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. (HPE) reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue and profit that surpassed Wall Street expectations on Monday, however, its share price slipped after-hours as its Q1 FY27 outlook fell short of the rosiest of Wall Street expectations.

For the quarter ended October 31, the Houston-based technology company posted revenue of $14.5 billion, up 50% from the same period a year earlier and ahead of the $14.3 billion average forecast from analysts polled by Fiscal.ai.

The cloud infrastructure firm reported earnings of $1.43 per share, beating the consensus projection of $1.28 a share. “We are now a fundamentally different company, with greater earnings power, a stronger competitive position, and a portfolio built to capitalize on the next phase of AI,” said Antonio Neri, president and CEO of HPE.

AI Servers And Juniper Integration Drive Growth

HPE’s rapid expansion was anchored by its Cloud & AI division, where quarterly revenue jumped 68.6% year-over-year to $11.3 billion and operating margins nearly doubled to 18.4% from 9.3%.

Within that unit, server revenue soared 94.7% to $8.8 billion on the back of demand for systems powered by Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.(AMD) processors, while storage revenue rose 33.8% to $1.5 billion.

The company’s networking segment, bolstered by its integration of Juniper Networks, generated $3.1 billion in revenue, representing a 12.3% increase over the prior year with an operating profit margin of 22.1%.

HPE Fiscal 2027 Earnings Guidance

HPE now projects fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 27% to 35% with revenues reaching as high as $63.1 billion, beating analyst expectations of $55.05 billion. Full-year adjusted earnings are projected to reach up to $5.35 per share.

For the current fiscal first quarter ending in January, HPE forecast revenue between $14 billion and $14.6 billion. While the bottom-line guidance comfortably exceeded Wall Street’s average estimate of $1.08 per share, the top-line range fell just shy of the most bullish analyst projections of $14.7 billion, tempering investor enthusiasm.

data.title: Jyong Biotech Announces Receipt of Letter of Intent from a Philippine Enterprise to Explore Commercialization of Investigational Innovative Drug in the Philippines
data.description:
NEW TAIPEI CITY, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jyong Biotech Ltd. (Nasdaq: MENS) (the "Company" or "Jyong Biotech"), a science-driven biotechnology company dedicated to the development and commercialization of innovative plant-derived therapeutics, today announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Health Ever Bio-Tech Co., Ltd., has entered into a Letter of Intent ("LOI") with a Philippine healthcare enterprise. The LOI initiates an evaluation of a potential collaboration for the in-licensing, development, and commercialization of Jyong Biotech's investigational new drug in the Philippines.

Aligning with the Company's strategy to expand patient access in Southeast Asia, the LOI expresses the Philippine enterprise's intent to evaluate the potential in-licensing and distribution of Botreso®, an investigational therapy for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Through this potential collaboration, the Philippine enterprise expects to explore the Philippine regulatory pathway, market opportunities, and commercialization strategies for Botreso®.

According to the Global Burden of Disease (GBD 2021) and BMC Urology research, the global BPH patient population reached 112.5 million in 2021, representing an increase of over 122% from 50.7 million in 1990, and is projected to grow to between 150 million and 156 million by 2035. Despite this market growth, a significant unmet medical need remains due to the severe side effects and high discontinuation rates of existing treatments. Current BPH treatments primarily rely on medications such as alpha-blockers and 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (5-ARIs). However, these drugs are associated with a five-year discontinuation rate of 60% to 90% due to adverse effects like dizziness, orthostatic hypotension, ejaculatory dysfunction, and sexual dysfunction.

As an innovative botanical therapy, Botreso® aims to address this clinical gap. The drug has conducted four Phase III clinical trials in the U.S. and Taiwan, becoming the first Taiwanese-developed oral botanical new drug to advance to Phase III clinical trials with the U.S. FDA. Botreso® is being developed as a potential well-tolerated treatment option suitable for long-term use.

"Receiving this LOI from a Philippine enterprise marks an important step in our strategy to evaluate new markets for Botreso® in Southeast Asia," said Fu-Feng Kuo, Chairwoman and Chief Executive Officer of Jyong Biotech." Their experience in the Philippine regulatory landscape and commercial network make them a promising potential partner. We look forward to evaluating this opportunity as we advance the global commercialization of our innovative BPH treatments."

Headquartered in Metro Manila, the potential partner is a Philippine healthcare solutions company with established expertise in pharmaceutical regulatory affairs, product registration, market access, and commercialization. Its experience working with international pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturers and its relationships in the Philippine healthcare sector position it to support the potential introduction of Botreso® in the Philippines.

The LOI is non-binding, and there can be no assurance that any definitive agreement will be entered into. Any definitive agreement remains subject to due diligence, further evaluation of the product's clinical data, development status, regulatory requirements, and commercial terms. Moving forward, Jyong Biotech will continue leveraging its botanical platform to build a comprehensive BPH/LUTS portfolio centered on Botreso®, while accelerating the global development, out-licensing, and commercialization of its new drugs.

As of the date of this press release, Botreso® remains an investigational new drug candidate and has not been approved for commercial use in any jurisdiction.

About Jyong Biotech Ltd.

Headquartered in Taiwan, Jyong Biotech Ltd. is a science-driven biotechnology company committed to developing and commercializing innovative and differentiated new drugs (plant-derived), mainly specializing in the treatment of urinary system diseases, with an initial focus on the markets of the U.S., the EU and Asia. Since its inception in 2002, the Company has built integrated capabilities that encompass all key functionalities of drug development, including early-stage drug discovery and development, pharmacology, toxicology, clinical trials, regulatory affairs, manufacturing, and commercialization. Leveraging strong research and development capabilities and a proprietary platform, the Company has been developing a series of botanical drug candidates, including its primary botanical drug candidate, Botreso®, another clinical-stage botanical drug candidate, and other preclinical-stage botanical drug candidates. The Company endeavors to develop and supply first-class innovative drugs to meet customers' health needs and seeks to be a valuable business organization that is held in high esteem by the public. data.title: NVDA Shorts Lose $12B As Huang’s Return Erases Nearly 90% Of Recent Gains, Says S3 Partners
data.description:
Key points:
  • Short sellers collected about $13.7 billion in mark-to-market gains in the seven days that NVDA shares fell after Huang’s exit, including $5.9 billion on Friday alone. 
  • Even after Monday’s losses, short sellers remain up about $4 billion on Nvidia for 2026.
  • Nasdaq shorts, meanwhile, incurred an estimated $39 billion loss on Monday, more than reversing Friday’s profit.

Short sellers betting against Nvidia (NVDA) lost roughly $12 billion in a single session on Monday after the company’s shares jumped over 30% after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO, according to S3 Partners.

According to the analytics firm, the one-day hit wiped out nearly 90% of the gains those same short positions had built over the previous seven trading days. NVDA stock closed up 31.5% on Monday after the company reinstated Huang as CEO, causing a broader rally in tech and AI names that pushed the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index up 7%.

Seven Days Of Gains Vanish

After Huang stepped down following allegations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, Nvidia shares fell for seven straight sessions. Short sellers collected about $13.7 billion in mark-to-market gains during that stretch, including $5.9 billion on Friday alone when reports of the Securities and Exchange Commission probing the company’s accounting practices dragged the stock down.

The sharp rebound in NVDA shares on Monday pushed Nvidia’s short value at risk up 150% to $4.68 billion, the highest figure S3 Partners has recorded for any single stock.

Still Ahead For The Year—Barely

Even after Monday’s losses, short sellers remain up about $4 billion on Nvidia for 2026. The stock would need to reach roughly $173 to erase the gains from the seven-day decline and about $182 to wipe out the full year’s profit for the short side, the firm said.

Across Nasdaq names, short sellers had booked $83 billion in gains over the same seven sessions, $36 billion of it on Friday. On Monday, they incurred an estimated $39 billion loss, more than reversing Friday’s profit. Nasdaq shorts are now down about $64 billion for the year, the firm said.

How Did NVDA Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around NVDA stock stayed within the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing, accompanied by ‘extremely high’ retail chatter.

In an ongoing Stocktwits poll, nearly 64% of respondents said that they are more bullish on Nvidia now that Huang is back. 15% said they feel the same as before, while 9% said they are more bearish, and 12% voted that it's too early to tell.

NVDA stock has dropped 12% year-to-date.
